medications.name: Oxycodone
medications.frequency: Every 4-6 hours as needed for severe pain
medications.instructions: Take with food to prevent nausea. Do not drive or operate machinery. Taper off as shoulder pain improves.

medications.name: Ibuprofen
medications.instructions: Take scheduled for the first 5 days to reduce shoulder inflammation. Do not combine with other NSAIDs.

medications.name: Cyclobenzaprine
medications.instructions: Reduces shoulder and arm muscle spasms at night. Causes drowsiness — do not drive or drink alcohol.

restrictions.rule: Wear the shoulder sling at all times for the first 4 weeks, including while sleeping.
strict_prohibitions: No lifting anything heavier than a cup of water
No driving until sling is removed

restrictions.rule: Keep the surgical dressing clean and dry. You may shower after 48 hours with the shoulder wrapped in plastic.
strict_prohibitions: No submerging shoulder in water for 3 weeks

restrictions.rule: Pendulum exercises only during Week 1. PT-guided passive range of motion begins Week 2. Do not force arm above 60 degrees.

warning_signs.symptom: Sudden severe pain or complete loss of arm strength
warning_signs.implication: Possible nerve injury or suture failure
warning_signs.action: Go to the Emergency Room immediately

warning_signs.symptom: Hand or fingers turning blue, white, or cold
warning_signs.implication: Possible vascular compromise from sling pressure or swelling
warning_signs.action: Loosen the sling and go to the Emergency Room immediately

warning_signs.symptom: Fever over 101.5°F, chills, or increasing redness around the incision
Sudden shoulder swelling, severe bruising, or a popping sensation
warning_signs.action: Call Dr. Park's office or go to the Emergency Room
